title: What Is a Verified Measurement Credential? — Council of AI Answer-First Guide
context: 2026-09-25 EAT cycle — the verified measurement credential is the Council of AI's mechanism to tie a observed benchmark score back to the party that measured it. It distinguishes true negatives from parse noise, freezes the board state with an Ed25519-signed manifest, and makes monitored containment auditable rather than assumed.
body: A verified measurement credential is not a marketing badge. It is a cryptographic attestation that a particular model score on a particular measurement axis — for example, a detector-interop (det) score of 0.879 for one model versus 0.000 for another that could not parse the output format — was produced by a defined measurement process, with defined bank items (33–200 canonical cases), a defined model spread (19+ models), and an Ed25519-signed manifest that freezes the board state at a point in time. The credential answers three questions a deployer needs: (1) Who measured? (2) How was it measured? (3) Can I reproduce the observation? The Council of AI measurement board defines 14 axes — including detector interop, care, privacy, and adversarial robustness — each with a bank of items, a spread of scores, and a signed manifest. When a model's score shifts between measurements, the credential shows whether the shift reflects a true capability change or a measurement artefact (format failure, transport error, temperature drift, prompt variance). The verified measurement credential makes monitored containment practical: instead of claiming 'we built a safe system,' the deployer can point to a signed, append-only record of continuous observation and say 'we have continuous audit evidence that the containment boundary has been tested under these conditions, with these results, by this party.' The EU AI Act Article 9 risk-management and Article 50(2) machine-readable marking obligations both require evidence streams that can be inspected by regulators; the verification credential provides that stream without relying on unprovable isolation claims. It also protects insurers and underwriters: a credential that shows a model's worst-case spread (best to worst across the board) is far more informative than a single headline number.
